checks.correction: The rule, the 30 days (60 for organ transplants), the three options in 702(2) and the 3-business-day check grace in 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 3(3) are right. Two fixes. (1) Only Kentucky-licensed providers are protected: 304.17A-700(9) "'Health care provider' or 'provider' means a provider licensed in Kentucky"; a claim rendered by a clinician licensed only in Indiana cannot use 702/730. (2) Day 0 is receipt by the insurer or its claims processor 'at the address published by the insurer' (700(2)), and 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 3(5)(b) says the time frame does 'Not include the time a claim is with a health care clearinghouse acting on behalf of a provider'. The practice's own clearinghouse 999 acceptance is proof of transmittal, not the received date; use the payer's acknowledgment/277CA or the claim-status 'date the claim was received' (Sec. 2(2)(b)) to compute the due date and interest.

checks.quote: shall notify the provider, its billing agent, or designee that submitted the claim, in writing or electronically, of all information that is missing from the billing instrument, any errors in the billing instrument, or of any other circumstances which preclude it from being a clean claim.
checks.correction: Duties and deadlines are right (48 hours electronic, 20 calendar days paper, every defect named at acknowledgment, corrected clean claim adjudicated within the 702 time frame, claim status on the remittance or electronically). The stated consequence is not in the text: 704 sets no penalty and no 'deemed clean' rule for a defect not flagged at acknowledgment. It is an argument only, and a payer may still contest within 30 days under 706(3)(a) for 'information reasonably necessary', provided it gives 'an itemization of all new, never-before-provided information that is needed'. Letters should present it as an argument.

missing: KRS 304.17A-700(9) with 304.17A-005(23)(h); KRS 205.532(1)(g); KRS 205.646(1)(e): Kentucky prompt pay (304.17A-700 to 730), the Medicaid MCO duties in 205.532 to 205.536 and the Medicaid external review protect only a provider 'licensed in Kentucky' (700(9): "'Health care provider' or 'provider' means a provider licensed in Kentucky"). Claims of clinicians licensed only in Indiana cannot rely on them; the app should store each rendering clinician's Kentucky license and check it before citing Kentucky law. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=48419

KRS 304.17A-005(22)(a)7 and KRS 304.17A-603(1): Kentucky law reaches a 'Health benefit plan that affects the rights of a Kentucky insured and bears a reasonable relation to Kentucky, whether delivered or issued for delivery in Kentucky', and the UR, appeal and external review statutes 'apply to any insurer that covers citizens of the Commonwealth under a health benefit plan'. An Indiana resident on an Indiana-issued policy treated in Kentucky may fall outside Kentucky law; classify by plan situs and patient residence, not only by the clinic's state. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=54530

KRS 304.17A-700(2), 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 2(2)(b) and Sec. 3(5), KRS 304.17A-710(1)-(2): the 30-day clock runs from receipt 'at the address published by the insurer, whether it is the address of the insurer or a delegated claims processor'; time with the insurer's clearinghouse counts, time with the provider's clearinghouse does not; insurers must disclose the claims address, phone and delegated processors and give contracted providers 'thirty (30) calendar days' prior written notice' of changes (710(2)). Use the payer's received date (277CA or claim status), not the practice's clearinghouse 999 date, for due dates and interest. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=29334

KRS 304.17A-607(2)(l) and (4)(b) (text effective 7/15/2026) with 304.17A-613(6): a registered insurer or review agent must 'Comply with its own policies and procedures on file with the department', and 'No change to utilization review policies and procedures shall be effective or used until after it has been filed with and approved by the commissioner.' DOI must give a provider copies of the filed UR policies on request (613(6)); a denial resting on an unfiled new edit or criterion is a UR complaint under 613(8). https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57342

KRS 304.17A-600(16)(b): 'Retrospective review' 'Does not include the review of a claim that is limited to an evaluation of reimbursement levels, or adjudication of payment'. Pure payment-amount disputes are not utilization review and cannot go to Kentucky external review; route them through 304.17A-708(1) (no appeal may be required; 30 days) and 304.12-230(17). https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57341

KRS 304.17A-235(4): a material change that puts the practice into 'any new or modified insurance products, or proposes changes to the participating provider's membership networks' 'shall only take effect upon the acceptance of the participating provider, evidenced by a written signature' and must be 'sent by certified mail, return receipt requested'. A claim priced at a product or network rate the practice never signed for is an underpayment to dispute. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=45438

KRS 205.534(2) (effective 4/14/2026) with KRS 205.522(1)(m): Kentucky Medicaid MCO authorization requests must be approved within 24 hours (expedited) or 'within five (5) calendar days' (standard), extendable up to 14 days only at the enrollee's or provider's request or on justification to DMS; 205.522(1)(m) makes 304.17A-600, 603 and 607 apply to MCOs, including the deemed authorization in 607(3). Contract remedies (Aetna CY2026 Appendix A): row 59 '$500.00 per standard service authorization request for each day the Contractor is in default'; row 36 '$500.00 per day' for a late or non-compliant Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57033

KRS 205.536(1)-(2) with KRS 304.38-240: Medicaid MCO utilization review must use the medical necessity criteria designated by the Department of Insurance (one nationally recognized, objective, evidence-based set per category, not the MCO's proprietary criteria), and an MCO's private review agent 'shall comply with all applicable requirements of KRS 304.17A-600 to 304.17A-633'. Demand the criteria under 205.534(1)(a)3 and show where a denial departs from the designated set. Which set DOI designated was not checked. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=55333 and https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=47795

907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 6 (certified 2/5/2025): an appeal of a Medicaid MCO medical-necessity denial 'in a case involving a medical or surgical specialty or subspecialty, shall, upon request of the recipient, authorized person, or provider, include a review by a board-eligible or board-certified physician in the appropriate specialty or subspecialty area', and the reviewer 'shall not have participated in the initial review and denial'. Ask for a dermatologist, Mohs surgeon, dermatopathologist or radiation oncologist in every Kentucky Medicaid appeal. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/9950/document.engrossed.pdf

907 KAR 17:010 Sec. 5(5): at the enrollee's state fair hearing (requested within 120 days of the MCO's final letter, Sec. 5(3)), 'An automatic ruling shall be made by the department in favor of an enrollee if an MCO fails to' comply with the Sec. 4 appeal rules (for example the 30-day resolution), deliver its supporting documents within 5 days (Sec. 5(4)), or participate and present evidence. Usable only with the enrollee's specific written consent (Sec. 4(3)), and it bars a provider external review on the same claim (907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 2(4)). https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/11020/document.engrossed.pdf

Kentucky Medicaid MCO contract (verified in Aetna CY2026: Attachment C Sec. 34.0 item 1.G, Appendix I (e)(2), Appendix A row 73): the MCO must 'request and receive the Department's written permission to administratively collect overpayments in excess of $500'; failure to request it costs 'A forfeiture of the amount collected from the provider by the Contractor and a $10,000.00 penalty per occurrence.' On any program-integrity recoupment over $500, ask for DMS's written permission and copy DMS. Also Appendix A row 35: '$5,000.00 per occurrence per Enrollee' for 'Imposing arbitrary utilization guidelines, Prior Authorization restrictions ... not in accordance with an approved policy'. KRS 205.5356(4) obliges DMS to impose contract remedies once it finds a violation (contracts on or after 4/14/2026). https://www.chfs.ky.gov/agencies/dms/dhpo/Documents/CY2026Aetna.pdf

KRS 304.12-230(12): it is an unfair claims settlement practice to delay 'by requiring an insured, claimant, or the physician of either to submit a preliminary claim report and then requiring the subsequent submission of formal proof of loss forms, both of which submissions contain substantially the same information'. It names physicians; cite it against repeat requests for records already sent (fully insured and Medigap). https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=17037

806 KAR 17:370 Sec. 2-3 (effective 1/4/2022) with 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 2(1): when another payer is identified, a clean claim must include 'An explanation of benefits statement or noncoverage notice from another payer' or 'An electronic or paper-based Medicare remittance notice'; routinely requested attachments are limited to the listed standardized items. Attach the primary EOB or Medicare remittance to every secondary claim so the 30-day clock starts. https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/10592/document.engrossed.pdf

KRS 304.9-051(1)(a), 304.9-052(1), 304.99-020(1)(c), 304.2-160(3)-(4): a business that 'adjusts or settles claims on, residents of this state in connection with ... other life, health, or annuity benefit plans' is an 'administrator' that must hold a Kentucky license; administrators face civil penalties up to $2,000 per violation, and DOI indexes complaints by licensee and weighs them at renewal. A DOI complaint naming a TPA (for example UMR) is possible, but whether DOI will act on a self-funded ERISA plan's claim decision is not confirmed (29 U.S.C. 1144; DOI refers matters outside its jurisdiction). https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57325

DMS MCO contracts page (https://www.chfs.ky.gov/agencies/dms/dhpo/Pages/MCO-Contracts.aspx, read 11/23/2026): 'The Department for Medicaid Services contracts Aetna, Humana, Passport by Molina, UnitedHealthcare, and WellCare' and 'Anthem no longer participates in Kentucky Medicaid managed care.' The 2026-2027 contract renewals listed are for those five. Kentucky Medicaid citations (205.534, 205.646) apply to those five for current dates of service; Anthem appears only in the 2025-2026 and earlier contract lists, so an Anthem Medicaid claim is either an earlier Kentucky contract period or Indiana Medicaid (exit date not checked).
